data.description:
# Sound Module Index — catalogue every sound-node kind by primary function

**Work Item:** TF-0MV29HYZU001WUW7 | **Type:** docs | **Priority:** High

> **Summary:** Add a single, authoritative `docs/modules/index.md` that lists every
> ToneGraph sound-node kind ("sound module"), grouped by primary function, with a
> 2–3 sentence use-case description and availability status for each entry, and a
> test that keeps the index in sync with `ALLOWED_NODE_KINDS`.

## Problem Statement

ToneForge exposes its audio building blocks as ToneGraph **node kinds**
(`oscillator`, `noise`, `biquadFilter`, `envelope`, `lfo`, …), but there is no
single place that lists them all, grouped by what they are *for*, with guidance
on when a sound designer would reach for each one. Today a user must read the
flat "Supported Node Kinds" list in `docs/tonegraph.md`, then cross-reference the
parameter sections and the TypeScript interfaces in
`src/core/tonegraph-schema.ts`, to piece together the set of available modules
and their purpose. This costs time and risks the documentation silently drifting
from the code.

## Users

**Sound designers and gameplay/audio engineers** authoring ToneForge recipes and
ToneGraph documents, and **reviewers** who need to know at a glance what the
platform can synthesise.

### User Stories

- As a sound designer, I want one page that lists every sound-node kind grouped
  by function, so I can discover what building blocks are available without
  reading the full ToneGraph spec.
- As a recipe author, I want a short use-case description for each node kind, so
  I can quickly choose the right module (e.g. filtered noise vs. an FM pattern)
  for the sound I have in mind.
- As a maintainer, I want a test that fails when a new node kind is added to the
  code but not to the index, so the catalogue cannot drift out of date.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A new document `docs/modules/index.md` exists and is linked from the
   `README.md` § Documentation list.
2. The document lists **every** kind in `ALLOWED_NODE_KINDS`
   (`src/core/tonegraph-schema.ts`) — currently `destination`, `gain`,
   `oscillator`, `noise`, `biquadFilter`, `bufferSource`, `envelope`, `lfo`,
   `constant`, `fmPattern` — with **no omissions and no invented kinds**.
3. Entries are grouped under headings named by **primary function** (e.g.
   Generation, Filtering & tone shaping, Amplitude shaping, Modulation,
   Output & routing), and each kind appears exactly **once** under its primary
   group.
4. Each entry has a **2–3 sentence** description written for use cases — *when
   and why* to reach for the module — rather than only repeating its parameters.
5. Each entry states its **availability status** (e.g. "Implemented in ToneGraph
   v0.1") and links to the authoritative reference in `docs/tonegraph.md`
   (Kind Parameters) and/or the schema interface.
6. A Vitest test (`src/core/tonegraph-kinds-index.test.ts` or equivalent)
   asserts that the set of kinds in `docs/modules/index.md` equals
   `ALLOWED_NODE_KINDS` (no missing or unknown entries) and that every entry has
   a non-empty description; the test is the regression guard against drift.
7. `README.md` documentation links are updated and `docs/tonegraph.md` gains a
   "See also" cross-link to the new index.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant docs site entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Node kinds only.** The index covers ToneGraph node kinds (the "sound
  modules"). Top-level routing/sequencing constructs (`routes`, `buses`,
  `namespaces`, `sequences`, node automation) may be summarised in the
  introduction but are not modules and must not be presented as node kinds.
- **Single source of truth.** `ALLOWED_NODE_KINDS` in
  `src/core/tonegraph-schema.ts` is authoritative; the index must not introduce
  kinds the code does not accept.
- **No code behaviour change.** This is a documentation work item plus a
  read-only sync test; the audio path must not change.
- **Match existing docs conventions** — front-matter (`title`, `id`, `order`,
  `description`) as used by `docs/recipe-book/*.md`, and UK English spelling.

## Existing State

- No consolidated node-kind index exists.
- `docs/tonegraph.md` § "Supported Node Kinds (v0.1)" lists the ten kinds but
  only as a flat list; § "Kind Parameters" documents each kind's parameters.
- `src/core/tonegraph-schema.ts` defines `ALLOWED_NODE_KINDS` (the set of ten)
  and a typed interface per kind; it is the code source of truth.
- `src/core/tonegraph.ts` implements the loader for each kind, confirming all ten
  are implemented in v0.1.
- `README.md` § Architecture presents a *platform-module* layer table (Core,
  Stack, Sequencer, …) — related but a different concept from ToneGraph node
  kinds; the new index must not be confused with it.
- `docs/recipe-book/index.md` and `src/recipes/recipe-book.test.ts` are the
  precedent for a generated/curated docs index with a drift-catching test.

## Desired Change

1. Author `docs/modules/index.md`: an introduction explaining what a ToneGraph
   node kind is and how it relates to recipes; then function-grouped sections,
   each entry with a 2–3 sentence use-case description, availability status, and
   a link to `docs/tonegraph.md` and/or the schema interface.
2. Add the drift test asserting index ⇄ `ALLOWED_NODE_KINDS` parity.
3. Link the new page from `README.md` § Documentation and from
   `docs/tonegraph.md` ("See also").

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/modules/index.md` — **New.** The sound-module index, grouped by primary
  function with use-case descriptions and availability.
- `src/core/tonegraph-kinds-index.test.ts` — **New.** Vitest test asserting the
  index lists exactly `ALLOWED_NODE_KINDS`, and every entry has a description.
- `README.md` — Add a link to the new index under `## Documentation`.
- `docs/tonegraph.md` — Add a "See also" cross-link to `docs/modules/index.md`.
- `src/core/tonegraph-schema.ts` — Read-only reference: `ALLOWED_NODE_KINDS` and
  per-kind interfaces define what the index must cover.

## Related Work

- **Casual Game Recipe Book: 100 Documented Recipes (TF-0MUY9H7QZ000UX5W)** —
  precedent for a curated, test-guarded documentation index
  (`docs/recipe-book/index.md` + `src/recipes/recipe-book.test.ts`).
- **Review the 100 sound library documentation (TF-0MV290BG8003GXXH)** — adjacent
  open documentation task; the node-kind index complements the recipe catalogue.
- `docs/tonegraph.md` — authoritative ToneGraph v0.1 spec (node kinds, kinds,
  routing, automation) that the index summarises for discoverability.
- `docs/prd/CORE_PRD.md` — describes the recipe/synthesis model the node kinds
  serve.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption:** "Sound modules" (per operator decision) means ToneGraph node
  kinds, not ToneForge platform modules nor recipes.
- **Risk — doc/code drift:** kinds are added to the schema without updating the
  index. *Mitigation:* the sync test fails on any parity mismatch.
- **Risk — grouping bikeshedding:** a kind may plausibly fit two groups (e.g.
  `gain` under routing or amplitude). *Mitigation:* AC requires each kind appear
  exactly once; the entry text can mention secondary uses.
- **Risk — scope creep into sequencing:** the operator's examples mention
  "sequencing"; node kinds do not include a sequencer. *Mitigation:* keep the
  index to node kinds and describe `sequences`/automation only as context in the
  introduction.
- **Assumption:** all ten kinds are implemented in v0.1, so availability is
  uniformly "implemented"; the status field still captures future additions.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — What does "sound modules" mean for this index?** Options: (A) ToneForge
  platform modules, (B) ToneGraph sound-node kinds, (C) recipes/sound generators,
  (D) other.
  — **Answer (operator):** **1B — ToneGraph sound-node kinds** (the DSP building
  blocks available in a graph). Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 — Where should the index live?** Options: (A) new `docs/modules/index.md`
  linked from README, (B) extend the README architecture table, (C) new
  `docs/sound-module-index.md`.
  — **Answer (operator):** **2A — new `docs/modules/index.md`, linked from
  README**. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 — Coverage scope?** Options: (A) all modules marking implemented vs
  planned, (B) implemented modules only.
  — **Answer (operator):** **3A — all modules, marking implemented vs planned**.
  Source: interactive reply. Research: all ten v0.1 node kinds are implemented
  (`src/core/tonegraph.ts` loader dispatch), so the index records them as
  implemented and leaves room for future kinds.

- **TF-0MN06817414DW638** – Remove Tone.js dependency and unify on buildOfflineGraph (completed)
